title: Non-invertible SPT phases from fusion rings via Tannaka duality
authors: Antonio Santaniello, Roberto Valandro, Massimo Zorzenon
abstract: In a (1+1)-dimensional QFT with non-invertible symmetry, the fusion rules of topological lines are often the most accessible data, yet they do not fully determine whether the symmetry is anomaly-free, i.e. whether it admits trivially gapped phases. Such phases are characterized by fiber functors of the corresponding fusion category. Building on Tannaka duality, we extract fiber functors from the fusion ring alone by solving simultaneously for monoidal structure maps and tensor automorphisms. This allows us to find categorifications admitting a fiber functor without solving the pentagon equations directly. We test this procedure on the known Tambara--Yamagami ring of $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2$. Our main result concerns the rank-11 fusion ring shared by the representation categories of the two extraspecial groups of order 27, which has a multiplicity 3 channel and is relevant to self-triality. In both cases we find more than one fiber functor, i.e. several non-invertible SPT phases. We use the explicit data of these fiber functors to derive the $F$-symbols of the two representation categories in a compact form depending on a non-degenerate alternating bicharacter and an invertible object $ε$. Using the reconstructed data, we compute the anomalous algebra on the interface between two different SPT phases.
summary: This theoretical paper develops a powerful technique using Tannaka duality to classify non-invertible symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phases in 1+1D QFTs, using only the fusion ring data. By reconstructing fiber functors, the authors identify multiple distinct phases, providing explicit mathematical structures for their associated anomalies and interface algebras.
main_problem: The paper aims to determine if a symmetry in a (1+1)-dimensional QFT with non-invertible symmetry is anomaly-free, which is crucial for characterizing trivially gapped phases.
main_result: The authors developed a method using Tannaka duality to find multiple fiber functors, thereby identifying several non-invertible SPT phases, particularly for the fusion ring related to extraspecial groups of order 27.
method: They extract fiber functors directly from the fusion ring by solving for monoidal structure maps and tensor automorphisms, bypassing the direct solution of the pentagon equations.
model_or_system: The study focuses on (1+1)-dimensional Quantum Field Theories (QFTs) characterized by non-invertible symmetries, where the symmetry is implemented by topological line defects.
key_observables: Fiber functors, F-symbols, and the anomalous algebra computed on the interface between different SPT phases.
important_parameters: The structure of the fusion ring (e.g., the rank-11 ring from extraspecial groups) and invariants $(\epsilon, \iota)$ derived from the reconstruction.
main_assumptions: The procedure is tested on the maximal tensor-automorphism case, and the classification for $p>3$ is noted as conjectural.
figures_summary: The notes mention Table 4, which provides a comprehensive list of ring automorphisms used to generate all specific parametric forms associated with $	ext{Rep}(	ext{Esp}9)$.
paper_structure: The paper builds theory from fusion categories and Tannaka duality, develops a bootstrap procedure to find fiber functors from the fusion ring, applies this to known examples (Tambara-Yamagami), and concludes with explicit calculations for extraspecial groups.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical machinery connecting fusion rings to physical phases (SPT phases) is highly relevant for understanding topological order in condensed matter systems, providing tools to classify phases based on symmetry data.
